prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 2 columns and 1 row of equal 9:16 panels, 2 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: JI RAN'S OFFICE, Day, soft hazy daylight.
Image 1: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 2: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 3: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 4: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 5: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: The office is seen out of focus, with no person in frame. The one walnut desk stands before the floor-to-ceiling windows, which glow with soft daylight.
Panel 1: Wide shot, slow drift across the room, eye-level, shallow focus. The blurred office glows. Soft round points of light drift slowly across the image in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows.
Panel 2: Medium shot, slow push in toward the walnut desk, eye-level, shallow focus. The points of light swell and brighten as they float across the hazy walnut desk, until the frame turns bright.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
